dimension: Pasteboard privacy (macOS 15.4+/26/27 accessBehavior) and TCC permission timing
scenario: Facts baseline. Apple's NSPasteboard.AccessBehavior (macOS 15.4+) has cases alwaysAllow, alwaysDeny, ask and default; default for the General pasteboard is 'ask upon programmatic access'; other pasteboards (drag, service, find) stay open; an app is listed in Settings > Privacy & Security > Paste from Other Apps only after its first alert; alwaysDeny 'silently blocks'. Apple's page does not say what a read returns while a prompt is pending or after Deny. A third-party summary says the dev-preview default EnablePasteboardPrivacyDeveloperPreview is deprecated and inert in 27.2 beta 2, i.e. enforcement may arrive by default in a 27.x point update.
expected: Isla knows its own access state, or at least survives every state without silent loss.
actual_by_code: Sources contains no accessBehavior, detect*, or any denial handling (grep over Sources, Resources, Scripts, checklist.md is empty). The only repo record is docs/research/technical-feasibility.md:69 ('not active by default as of macOS 26.4'). Every pasteboard read is a plain string/data/readObjects call: ClipboardStore.swift:181,185,215,235,276,280,337; AppDelegate.swift:50.
steps: On this 27.0.1 Mac first open System Settings > Privacy & Security > Paste from Other Apps and see whether Isla (com.ctimothe.isla) is listed. Run `defaults read -g EnablePasteboardPrivacyDeveloperPreview` and `defaults read com.ctimothe.isla EnablePasteboardPrivacyDeveloperPreview`. This settles whether enforcement is already on. Then write the flag for com.ctimothe.isla only, relaunch through Scripts/install.sh, and run the next scenarios.

dimension: Pasteboard privacy (macOS 15.4+/26/27 accessBehavior) and TCC permission timing
scenario: ask mode, Clipboard History on (the default), user copies ordinary text in Safari while the panel is closed.
expected: At most one explained prompt, or none because Isla probes types first.
actual_by_code: Timer fires every 0.5 s (ClipboardStore.swift:119). pollNow sees changeCount moved (:175), then performs data(forType: .islaInternal) at :181 and readObjects at :185 and string(forType:) at :215 before anything is explained to the user. Under ask each changed pasteboard can raise 'Isla is trying to access the pasteboard' once per copy; there is no pre-prompt screen, the welcome pane copy (WelcomePane.swift:41-49) never mentions the clipboard, and history is on by default (NotchViewModel.swift:630-634), so the first alert arrives unexplained with the panel closed.
steps: Enable the dev-preview flag for com.ctimothe.isla, relaunch, copy text in Safari five times a minute apart. Record: does an alert appear on every copy; does Allow apply once only; what does the alert say; is the alert attributed to 'Isla'.

dimension: Pasteboard privacy (macOS 15.4+/26/27 accessBehavior) and TCC permission timing
scenario: ask mode: is the read synchronous? A copy is made and the alert is on screen unanswered.
expected: The main thread stays responsive.
actual_by_code: pollNow runs on the main actor inside the timer callback (ClipboardStore.swift:119-121). If the OS blocks the reading thread until the alert is answered, the main thread freezes: PointerWatcher sampling, hot keys (GlobalHotKey callbacks), hover brightening, ambient moments, the media ticker and lock-state handling all stop until the user answers. The panel is an accessory window and shows nothing about why. Nothing in the code reads off the main thread or with a timeout.
steps: With ask enabled, copy text, leave the alert unanswered for 20 s, and meanwhile hover the island, press the open-panel hot key, and check whether the cursor over the notch reacts. Then answer and compare.

dimension: Pasteboard privacy (macOS 15.4+/26/27 accessBehavior) and TCC permission timing
scenario: ask mode, alternative branch: the read returns nil immediately while the alert shows, then the user clicks Allow.
expected: The copy that triggered the alert is still recorded after Allow.
actual_by_code: lastChangeCount is advanced at ClipboardStore.swift:176 before any read. If string(forType:) returns nil, the guard at :215-216 returns silently and nothing re-polls that change count. The copy that caused the prompt is lost permanently even though the user allowed access. The same ordering loses image copies (encodeImage nil path, :303-319 then :335-341). No retry keyed on 'read denied' exists.
existing_test: ClipboardStoreTests uses a private pasteboard that never denies; none for nil-after-change

dimension: Pasteboard privacy (macOS 15.4+/26/27 accessBehavior) and TCC permission timing
scenario: alwaysDeny (user picked Deny in Paste from Other Apps, or a managed Mac forces it). Copy text anywhere.
expected: Clipboard tab says why it is empty and links to the setting; or the poll stops.
actual_by_code: Reads return nil/empty (per Apple 'silently blocks'). pollNow records nothing (:215-217). ClipboardPane shows a bare glyph; the only explanatory text is for history switched off (ClipboardPane.swift:9-17). The 0.5 s timer keeps running forever. Settings Privacy has no status row and Copy Diagnostics prints only 'Clipboard History: on' (Diagnostics.swift:98), so a support report cannot show the cause. History appears broken with no message.
steps: Set Isla to Don't Allow in Paste from Other Apps (or enable the flag and press Deny). Copy text five times, open the Clipboard tab. Expect and record: empty list, no message. Then open Settings and Copy Diagnostics and confirm the report shows no pasteboard state.

dimension: Pasteboard privacy (macOS 15.4+/26/27 accessBehavior) and TCC permission timing
scenario: alwaysDeny with Save Clipboard Screenshots on: user takes a screenshot to clipboard.
expected: Isla recognises denial and stops retrying, or tells the user once.
actual_by_code: availableType(from:[.png,.tiff]) is non-nil (types are visible, :206), so encodeImage runs (:207). data(forType: .png) and .tiff both return nil (:276,:280). The code treats nil as 'bytes not here yet' and retries every 0.5 s up to 12 attempts (:303-319), each attempt doing two gated reads, so up to 26 denied reads over about 6 s, then recordTextFallback finds nothing (:335-341). Under ask each retry may re-raise the alert. The comment at :271-274 assumes nil means a Continuity delay; denial is indistinguishable.
steps: Deny Isla, turn on Save Clipboard Screenshots, press Shift-Control-Command-4 (to clipboard), watch Console for alert count and whether ~/Pictures/Isla gains a file. Repeat in ask mode and count alerts during the 6 s window.

dimension: Pasteboard privacy (macOS 15.4+/26/27 accessBehavior) and TCC permission timing
scenario: ask mode with History OFF and Save Clipboard Screenshots ON: user copies plain text.
expected: Text copies are never read when only images are wanted.
actual_by_code: refreshClipboardPolling keeps the timer alive (NotchStores.swift:150-157) because images are wanted. pollNow still runs data(forType:.islaInternal) at :181 and readObjects(forClasses:[NSURL]) at :185 for every changed pasteboard, before consulting wantsImages (:198) or recordsHistory (:214). NSURL reading can coerce string data, so a text-only copy may be a gated read and raise an alert although the user switched history off. The comment at :213 'History off: text is not even read' is only true of the final string read.
steps: ask enabled; History off, Save Clipboard Screenshots on; copy text; see whether an alert appears. If it does, reordering to an availableType(from:) gate before any data read is the fix.

dimension: Pasteboard privacy (macOS 15.4+/26/27 accessBehavior) and TCC permission timing
scenario: Hot key Control-Option-Command-T (translate clipboard) under ask and under alwaysDeny.
expected: Either a read after an explained prompt, or visible feedback that the clipboard could not be read.
actual_by_code: AppDelegate.swift:49-52 reads NSPasteboard.general.string from a Carbon hot key callback, not from paste UI, so it is a programmatic read. Under ask the alert appears over whatever app is frontmost; under alwaysDeny string is nil and the closure returns at :50 with no sound, panel or message. The comment at AppDelegate.swift:36-41 and the inventory line 'Hotkey: no permission' are untrue for this key once pasteboard privacy is on.
steps: With the flag on, copy text in Notes, press the hot key. Record the alert text and where it appears. Press Deny and repeat: confirm nothing visible happens.

dimension: Pasteboard privacy (macOS 15.4+/26/27 accessBehavior) and TCC permission timing
scenario: Command-V in the Translate field under ask/alwaysDeny.
expected: A user's own Command-V is treated as a user-initiated paste and works without an alert.
actual_by_code: NotchPanel.sendEvent intercepts keyDown Command-V (NotchPanel.swift:100-105) and calls firstResponder.tryToPerform(NSText.paste) (:124-126) because the accessory app has no Edit menu. Apple exempts access resulting from 'input on a UI element the system considers paste-related'. A paste action synthesised from a custom sendEvent with no NSMenuItem may not be recognised, so a deliberate paste could prompt, or be silently empty under alwaysDeny. The right-click Paste of the NSTextView menu would be recognised normally.
steps: ask and alwaysDeny in turn: copy text in Notes, open Translate, click the field, press Command-V, then repeat with right-click > Paste. Record alert/no-alert and whether text lands.

dimension: Pasteboard privacy (macOS 15.4+/26/27 accessBehavior) and TCC permission timing
scenario: Services item 'Translate in Isla' and drag pasteboards under pasteboard privacy.
expected: Unaffected, because these are not the General pasteboard.
actual_by_code: translateSelection reads the pasteboard macOS passes in (AppDelegate.swift:105-111), a service pasteboard. Shelf drops read sender.draggingPasteboard (NotchRootView.swift:338-343). Apple states all other pasteboards allow access.
steps: With alwaysDeny on, select text in TextEdit and run Services > Translate in Isla, then drag a Finder file onto the island. Both should still work.

dimension: Pasteboard privacy (macOS 15.4+/26/27 accessBehavior) and TCC permission timing
scenario: Concealed copy from a password manager under ask.
expected: No alert and no read for a ConcealedType copy.
actual_by_code: pollNow checks availableType(from: optOut) at :178, which comes before every data read (:181 onward). If 'types' is not gated, the secret never triggers an alert. If availableType itself is gated, the alert would fire for secrets too, and the order would not help. Only the first case is a code fact.
steps: ask on; copy a password in 1Password/Keychain Access; confirm no alert for that copy while a normal copy does alert.

dimension: Pasteboard privacy (macOS 15.4+/26/27 accessBehavior) and TCC permission timing
scenario: Isla copies something itself (Shelf Copy, Copy Line, Copy translation, Copy Diagnostics) under ask.
expected: Own writes never raise an alert about Isla reading its own data.
actual_by_code: ClipboardStore.copy re-baselines lastChangeCount (:166), so row copy-backs are not re-read. ShelfStore.copy (ShelfStore.swift:369-381), Translator.copyOutput (Translator.swift:566-570), LyricRow copy (LyricRow.swift:105-106) and Diagnostics (Diagnostics.swift:152-155) do not, so the next poll reads them: data(forType:.islaInternal) at ClipboardStore.swift:181 on Isla's own write. Whether the OS exempts same-process reads is unknown.
steps: ask on; press Copy on a translation result, Copy Line on a lyric, Copy on a Shelf image card; note any alert naming Isla.

dimension: Pasteboard privacy (macOS 15.4+/26/27 accessBehavior) and TCC permission timing
scenario: Copy Translate result with the Translate privacy cover on.
expected: The translation does not become a readable history row.
actual_by_code: Translator.copyOutput writes plain .string with no TransientType or islaInternal marker (Translator.swift:566-570). The poll then records it as an ordinary entry (ClipboardStore.swift:215-217) in the Clipboard tab. The Translate cover hides only the Translate pane; the Clipboard cover is a separate, default-off switch (inventory, PrivacyMode). Lyric Copy Line (LyricRow.swift:105) behaves the same.

dimension: Pasteboard privacy (macOS 15.4+/26/27 accessBehavior) and TCC permission timing
scenario: Pasting a bare path or file URL copied as text (for example `pwd | pbcopy`, or text 'file:///Users/me/a.txt') into history.
expected: Recorded as the text that was copied.
actual_by_code: pollNow tries readObjects(forClasses:[NSURL], .urlReadingFileURLsOnly) first (ClipboardStore.swift:184-196) and, if any file URL comes back, records a .file entry and returns without reading the string. NSURL pasteboard reading accepts string types, so a text copy that parses as a file URL may be recorded as a file row (doc icon, name only) and copied back as a file reference (:161-162) instead of the text. Not traced to the AppKit side.

dimension: Pasteboard privacy (macOS 15.4+/26/27 accessBehavior) and TCC permission timing
scenario: Universal Clipboard FILE copy from another Mac or iPhone Files app, history on.
expected: The poll never blocks the main thread on a remote transfer.
actual_by_code: readObjects NSURL at ClipboardStore.swift:185 on main may force Continuity to materialise the file URL; for a promise-backed file the call can wait on the network. Existing rows cover Universal Clipboard text and images, not files. After the read the entry stores a temporary URL (.file) that may be cleaned by the system later, so copy-back from history later writes a dead reference.
steps: Copy a 500 MB file in Finder on a second Mac signed into the same Apple ID; watch Isla's main thread (Activity Monitor sample) and the pointer hover response during the transfer.

dimension: Pasteboard privacy (macOS 15.4+/26/27 accessBehavior) and TCC permission timing
scenario: Pasteboard state at wake/unlock while a prompt could appear.
expected: No alert appears on the lock screen or over a sleeping display.
actual_by_code: Polling stops on lock/sleep (NotchStores.swift:138-139) and resumes via refreshClipboardPolling (:197) which uses start(), keeping the old baseline (ClipboardStore.swift:113-118). On unlock the first poll reads whatever changed during the lock, a programmatic read that under ask raises an alert about a copy the user did not make in this session (and see G-011 for the recording side).
steps: ask on; lock the Mac, send a Universal Clipboard copy from the phone, unlock, look for an alert.

dimension: Pasteboard privacy (macOS 15.4+/26/27 accessBehavior) and TCC permission timing
scenario: macOS point update flips the default (27.0.1 to 27.2 or later) with no Isla change.
expected: Behaviour is verified per OS build, not assumed.
actual_by_code: Nothing in scripts/check or the Scripts/test-*.sh gates exercises pasteboard access; ClipboardStoreTests uses NSPasteboard(name:) private pasteboards that are never gated. A silent loss of Clipboard history and clipboard screenshots would pass the whole gate.

dimension: Pasteboard privacy (macOS 15.4+/26/27 accessBehavior) and TCC permission timing
scenario: Ad-hoc signed update replaces the app (README/DMG users, and the owner's own Scripts/install.sh loop). All earlier TCC grants.
expected: checklist.md and RecordingPickup.swift:21-24 say 'the grant sticks'.
actual_by_code: Releases are ad-hoc (checklist.md:614-616; bundle.sh:207 SIGN_IDENTITY defaults to '-'). TCC records an ad-hoc binary by cdhash, which changes on every build, so Desktop, Documents, Downloads, Automation (Music, Spotify), Accessibility and any Paste-from-Other-Apps Allow are forgotten at each update. Every update replays the whole prompt set, and the Desktop and Automation prompts may arrive at launch (see below) rather than in context. The owner's rebuild-after-every-change loop (CLAUDE.md step 2-3) means this machine sees them constantly.
steps: `tccutil reset All com.ctimothe.isla`, install build A, grant Desktop and Music; rebuild with a trivial change and Scripts/install.sh; `codesign -dv --verbose=4 /Applications/Isla.app` to compare CDHash; relaunch and list which prompts return.

dimension: Pasteboard privacy (macOS 15.4+/26/27 accessBehavior) and TCC permission timing
scenario: Helper refused (Gatekeeper, the common DMG case) with Music or Spotify running: first launch.
expected: checklist.md:36 'Nothing is requested at launch.'
actual_by_code: NowPlayingFeed reports unavailable, MediaController.switchToScriptingFallback calls refreshFromPlayers() at once (MediaController.swift:1790), which goes PlayerBridge.currentState to stateReply to runScript for each running player (PlayerBridge.swift:104-121,66-69). That is an Apple Event to Music and/or Spotify with the panel closed, so the Automation prompt appears at launch, two in a row if both run. Distinct from G-005, which is the Spotify track-id lookup on the helper route.
steps: Reset Automation (`tccutil reset AppleEvents com.ctimothe.isla`), quarantine a copy so the helper is refused (xattr -w com.apple.quarantine), start Spotify playing, launch Isla, and note whether a prompt appears with no panel open.

dimension: Pasteboard privacy (macOS 15.4+/26/27 accessBehavior) and TCC permission timing
scenario: Automation prompt is up and unanswered; the user taps Play/Pause or Next on the island.
expected: Transport taps still work or fail fast.
actual_by_code: All scripts share one serial queue (PlayerBridge.swift:402,'queue'; runScript :484 onward). executeAndReturnError blocks that thread while the TCC prompt is pending, so a later .transport script waits behind it (the yield logic at :476-482 only skips queued polls, it cannot interrupt the running one). The icon flips at once (MediaController.swift:860-867) and reverts after the 1.5 s confirmation timer. If the prompt is ignored the queue is wedged until the AE timeout.
steps: Reset Automation, launch Isla on the fallback route with Music running, leave the prompt up, open the panel and tap Next five times. Record whether anything reaches Music after Allow.

dimension: Pasteboard privacy (macOS 15.4+/26/27 accessBehavior) and TCC permission timing
scenario: Spotify denied, Music allowed and open with a paused track (fallback route).
expected: The island shows Spotify's playing song or an explicit 'cannot ask Spotify'.
actual_by_code: currentState (PlayerBridge.swift:104-121) maps both .unknown (-1743 denied) and .empty to nil because state(of:) forwards only .loaded (:73-77). Results then contain only Music's paused track and results.first(where: isPlaying) ?? results.first returns it, so the island shows a stale paused Music track while Spotify plays. The -1743 code is documented in comments (:394) and never surfaced.

dimension: Pasteboard privacy (macOS 15.4+/26/27 accessBehavior) and TCC permission timing
scenario: User denies Automation once, then wants to enable it.
expected: Settings says what is blocked and links to Privacy & Security > Automation.
actual_by_code: No call to AEDeterminePermissionToAutomateTarget and no -1743 handling in Sources (grep). macOS never re-prompts after Deny, so the only remedy is a Settings pane the app never points to. The Music tab only says 'Only Music and Spotify can be seen right now' (inventory). Round-1 ledger row covers the fallback-only case; this adds the helper-route consequence: precisionPlayer, modes and the heart stay off with no explanation.

dimension: Pasteboard privacy (macOS 15.4+/26/27 accessBehavior) and TCC permission timing
scenario: Spotify track-id lookup keeps retrying after Automation was denied.
expected: Stops after the first -1743.
actual_by_code: requestSpotifyTrackID (MediaController.swift:624-631) retries with 1, 2, 4, 8 s back-off per track regardless of the failure code, so a denied Spotify costs four failed Apple Events per track change for the whole session and a log line each (PlayerBridge.swift:494-498).

dimension: Pasteboard privacy (macOS 15.4+/26/27 accessBehavior) and TCC permission timing
scenario: System media-key fallback with no Accessibility permission.
expected: Visible failure, or a one-time request that lists Isla in Privacy & Security > Accessibility.
actual_by_code: dispatch ends in PlayerBridge.postMediaKey (MediaController.swift:1011-1017 reaches PlayerBridge.swift:206-221), which posts a CGEvent to cghidEventTap. The code never calls AXIsProcessTrusted or AXIsProcessTrustedWithOptions, and Info.plist has no related key (bundle.sh:85-92). Unprompted, Isla never appears in the Accessibility list, so the user cannot even enable it by hand without the + button. The docstring (:204-205) says 'silently does nothing'. Reached by the Play/Pause, Next and Previous intents (IslaIntents.swift:173-180) with no player and no helper.
steps: Quit Music, Spotify and all players, break the helper (quarantine), run the Play or Pause shortcut. Check Accessibility list for Isla, and whether any prompt appeared.

dimension: Pasteboard privacy (macOS 15.4+/26/27 accessBehavior) and TCC permission timing
scenario: Media-key fallback WITH Accessibility granted and nothing playing.
expected: No unrelated app starts.
actual_by_code: A synthesised NX_KEYTYPE_PLAY system key (PlayerBridge.swift:206-221) is handled by macOS like a keyboard key; with no active Now Playing client, the system launches Apple Music. The intent returns success with no result text.
steps: Grant Accessibility, quit all players, run the Play or Pause shortcut, see whether Music opens.

dimension: Pasteboard privacy (macOS 15.4+/26/27 accessBehavior) and TCC permission timing
scenario: Global mouse-down monitor while the panel is pinned (macOS 26/27).
expected: No Input Monitoring prompt or entry.
actual_by_code: NSEvent.addGlobalMonitorForEvents for leftMouseDown and rightMouseDown (NotchController.swift:737-739). Mouse events historically need no Input Monitoring (key events do). No scenario records that this still holds on 27.0.1. If the monitor stops delivering, a pinned panel would never close on an outside click.
steps: Press Control-Option-Command-I (pins), click in another app, confirm the panel folds. Then check Privacy & Security > Input Monitoring for an Isla entry.

dimension: Pasteboard privacy (macOS 15.4+/26/27 accessBehavior) and TCC permission timing
scenario: Global hot keys (RegisterEventHotKey) on 27.0.1.
expected: No Accessibility or Input Monitoring prompt, as promised.
actual_by_code: GlobalHotKey.swift:8 uses Carbon registration with no event tap; the shortcut recorder uses a local monitor only (HotKeys.swift:277). Matches the promise.
steps: On a freshly reset account press all three keys; confirm no TCC dialog.

dimension: Pasteboard privacy (macOS 15.4+/26/27 accessBehavior) and TCC permission timing
scenario: Launch with Save Clipboard Screenshots OFF (default): what Isla writes to ~/Pictures.
expected: Nothing is created until the feature is switched on (NotchViewModel.swift:620-627 says keeping clipboard copies is the user's decision).
actual_by_code: NotchStores.init builds ScreenshotVault() unconditionally (NotchStores.swift:46), and ScreenshotVault.init calls resolveFolder, which runs createDirectory on ~/Pictures/Isla (ScreenshotVault.swift:18-44,28-38). The empty folder appears at every first launch with the feature off. If Pictures is relocated to a network or removable volume that is a launch-time access (and prompt).

dimension: Pasteboard privacy (macOS 15.4+/26/27 accessBehavior) and TCC permission timing
scenario: Screenshot.app saves to ~/Pictures/Shots (not the Desktop); first Shelf open.
expected: Only the configured folder is scanned and prompted for.
actual_by_code: captureFolders always appends the Desktop (RecordingPickup.swift:209-212), then stores the merged list back to defaults (:217). So the Desktop prompt appears at the first Shelf open even if the user has never saved anything to the Desktop, with the usage text 'Isla shows new screenshots and recordings saved to the Desktop' (InfoPlist.strings:5), which is false for that user.

dimension: Pasteboard privacy (macOS 15.4+/26/27 accessBehavior) and TCC permission timing
scenario: captures.folders only grows.
expected: A folder that no longer exists, or a retired external volume, drops out.
actual_by_code: captureFolders merges current + stored + Desktop, de-duplicates and writes back (RecordingPickup.swift:205-218). No removal path exists in Sources. Each folder is scanned on every Shelf open (ShelfStore.swift:216-229). A volume the user once pointed Screenshot.app at (USB, SMB) is retried forever: mounted removable volume gives a removable-volumes prompt, a stalled SMB mount blocks the main thread inside contentsOfDirectory (RecordingPickup.swift:56-60).

dimension: Pasteboard privacy (macOS 15.4+/26/27 accessBehavior) and TCC permission timing
scenario: Usage descriptions for removable volumes, network volumes and File Provider / iCloud Drive.
expected: Every prompt Isla can cause explains itself in en and ru.
actual_by_code: Info.plist declares only NSAppleEventsUsageDescription, NSDesktopFolderUsageDescription, NSDocumentsFolderUsageDescription, NSDownloadsFolderUsageDescription (Scripts/bundle.sh:85-92). No NSRemovableVolumesUsageDescription, NSNetworkVolumesUsageDescription, or NSFileProviderDomainUsageDescription, although shelf cards, remembered capture folders and watched lyrics folders can all sit on those (Dropbox/OneDrive in ~/Library/CloudStorage, /Volumes/*, smb). The system then shows its generic English text, unlocalized. test-localizations.sh (line 22) checks only keys that exist.

dimension: Pasteboard privacy (macOS 15.4+/26/27 accessBehavior) and TCC permission timing
scenario: Usage text does not match the caller: Documents or Downloads prompt raised by the lyrics-folder scan.
expected: The text explains why this prompt is appearing.
actual_by_code: The only Documents text is 'Isla shows files you put on the Shelf from Documents.' (InfoPlist.strings:6), but a watched lyrics folder under Documents is scanned at launch (LocalLyricsLibrary.swift:159,261-281) and by installFolderWatchers (:572-587). The user sees a Shelf sentence at launch with no Shelf and no panel. Round-1 ledger records the launch prompt; the mismatch of text and caller is new.

dimension: Pasteboard privacy (macOS 15.4+/26/27 accessBehavior) and TCC permission timing
scenario: Launch prompt blocks installation of the hot keys and the panel.
expected: A pending TCC prompt cannot stop the app from becoming usable.
actual_by_code: applicationDidFinishLaunching builds the controller at AppDelegate.swift:19; NotchController's NotchStores property runs LocalLyricsLibrary.init, which enumerates the folder synchronously (LocalLyricsLibrary.swift:159). Only after it returns do install() (:20), HotKeyCenter.install (:47) and the welcome timer (:69-73) run. A protected-folder prompt left open therefore delays the hot keys and the island, and a login-item start can sit behind the login screen's alerts.
steps: Add a lyrics folder under ~/Documents, quit, `tccutil reset SystemPolicyDocumentsFolder com.ctimothe.isla`, launch, leave the prompt unanswered 30 s and try the hot key and hover.

dimension: Pasteboard privacy (macOS 15.4+/26/27 accessBehavior) and TCC permission timing
scenario: Shelf Desktop prompt answered Don't Allow, then Allow later in System Settings.
expected: Captures taken meanwhile arrive once, in order.
actual_by_code: A denied scan yields [] via try? (RecordingPickup.swift:56-60), so seen stays empty and recordings.since stays at install time. After a later grant, every capture since install (not since grant) is offered at once; add() sorts and caps at 60 (ShelfStore.swift:250-265), silently dropping older ones. No message at any step; the Settings row 'Show Screen Captures' stays on throughout.

dimension: Pasteboard privacy (macOS 15.4+/26/27 accessBehavior) and TCC permission timing
scenario: Denied Desktop/Documents/Downloads: any way to tell?
expected: Settings or the Shelf says captures cannot be read, with a link to Files and Folders.
actual_by_code: importNewRecordings swallows the failure (ShelfStore.swift:216-229) and refreshFromDisk treats non-ENOENT errors as 'not gone' (isGone, ShelfStore.swift:233-241) so cards stay. Promise at checklist.md:128-132 ('denied means the shelf shows what it holds') is met, but nothing reports the denial anywhere; Diagnostics has no TCC state.

dimension: Pasteboard privacy (macOS 15.4+/26/27 accessBehavior) and TCC permission timing
scenario: Pasteboard read from the Shelf drag callbacks and file promise path.
expected: Unaffected by pasteboard privacy; TCC only on the destination folder.
actual_by_code: Reads use draggingPasteboard (NotchRootView.swift:338-343) and write promises to Application Support/Dropped (AppPaths.swift:47-56), which TCC does not guard. Handled for both gates.
steps: Drag a Photos item and a Mail attachment with alwaysDeny set; confirm cards appear.

dimension: Pasteboard privacy (macOS 15.4+/26/27 accessBehavior) and TCC permission timing
scenario: Shelf drop of a Downloads/Documents file when the folder's TCC state is undetermined.
expected: A dragged file needs no folder prompt.
actual_by_code: ShelfStore.add calls NSWorkspace.icon(forFile:) and QLThumbnailGenerator (ShelfStore.swift:249,266-280) and makeBookmark at persist (:419-430) on the dropped file in the drag-accept callback (NotchViewModel.accept :985-991). Whether TCC treats a dragged item as user-granted access for these calls (especially the thumbnail daemon acting for Isla) is not established.
steps: tccutil reset SystemPolicyDownloadsFolder com.ctimothe.isla; with a fresh Isla, drag one Downloads file to the island; note whether a Downloads prompt appears and whether a thumbnail renders.

dimension: Pasteboard privacy (macOS 15.4+/26/27 accessBehavior) and TCC permission timing
scenario: Bookmark resolution at launch for cards in a TCC-protected folder.
expected: No prompt before the Shelf is opened (checklist.md:204).
actual_by_code: ShelfStore.load resolves each bookmark at launch (ShelfStore.swift:108-166) with .withoutUI/.withoutMounting. The comment concedes it 'touches the filesystem'. Whether resolution of a Desktop/Documents/Downloads bookmark triggers a TCC check is not shown in the repo; the checklist item at :204 is unchecked.
steps: Put a Downloads card on the shelf, quit, reset SystemPolicyDownloadsFolder, relaunch without opening the panel, watch for a prompt.

dimension: Pasteboard privacy (macOS 15.4+/26/27 accessBehavior) and TCC permission timing

dimension: Local lyric editor, local lyrics library, per-track timing nudge persistence and the one-time legacy migration (round 2)
scenario: Word-timed enhanced LRC with a positive [offset:+500]: the user opens Edit Lyrics and presses Save Copy (or Export) without changing anything, repeatedly.
expected: A no-op save reproduces the same timings, and line and word times stay consistent with each other.
actual_by_code: parse() subtracts the offset from line stamps only (LocalLyricsDocument.swift:98-102), while words keep their raw stamps (:186). serialize() then adds the offset back to BOTH line and word stamps (:117, :122). Each Save Copy therefore moves every word +offset later while lines return to their original stamp. Even before saving, words are absolute and lines are offset-shifted, so the karaoke sweep (LyricSweep.wordFraction compares position to word.at, LyricSweep.swift:140-146) starts `offset` late relative to its line.

dimension: Local lyric editor, local lyrics library, per-track timing nudge persistence and the one-time legacy migration (round 2)
scenario: Word-timed enhanced LRC with a negative offset ([offset:-300]) whose first word starts on the line stamp, the usual layout. The user presses Save Copy or Export.
expected: The save succeeds, or fails with a reason the user can act on.
actual_by_code: Words are not offset-adjusted on parse (:186) but serialize writes word.at + offset (:122), so the first word is emitted 0.3 s BEFORE its own line stamp. The re-parse inside LocalLyricsDraft.document() (LocalLyricsEditor.swift:32) then trips `timestamp >= lineStart` (LocalLyricsDocument.swift:178) and throws invalidTimestamp. The sheet shows 'This LRC file is invalid.' (LocalLyricsEditorView.swift:153) for a file that imported fine.

dimension: Local lyric editor, local lyrics library, per-track timing nudge persistence and the one-time legacy migration (round 2)

The karaoke gate is `granularity == .word` (LyricsPresentation.swift:85), so word karaoke is off for the entire song although every other line still carries words.

dimension: Local lyric editor, local lyrics library, per-track timing nudge persistence and the one-time legacy migration (round 2)

actual_by_code: Out of order: parse throws invalidTimestamp (:92) and the UI shows 'This LRC file is invalid.' with no row (LocalLyricsEditorView.swift:152-154). Negative: formatTimestamp clamps with max(0, time) (:217), so -3 is silently saved as 00:00.00, and fails the order check if an earlier row is above 0. Duplicates: `timestamp < lastTimestamp` is strict, so equal stamps save, and the stage then shares one row id per stamp (F-010). The same string is shown for I/O failures (:167-169).

dimension: Upgrade and data compatibility; network etiquette (round 2 gap)
scenario: While an LRCLIB lookup has failed and its three retries are spent, the lyrics folder keeps changing (a sync client touching files).
expected: Failures are throttled; a rescan never bypasses the retry budget.
actual_by_code: Each rescan that changes state advances library.revision (LocalLyricsLibrary.swift:300-ish rescan tail, advanceRevision :606-608). LyricsCoordinator subscribes (:135-138) and recheckCurrentTrack runs resolveCurrentTrack (:271-283) into lookUpOnlineIfNeeded (:291-312). A failed outcome is not cached (OnlineLyrics.swift:345), so each revision sends a fresh exact request (plus searches) even after scheduleRetry's guard has stopped (:170). The retryAttempt counter is not reset or consulted on this path. Hold-up depends on how often files change. The same applies to every Retry press (:188-192).
steps: Counting transport that fails; call the library's rescan with a changing folder ten times after the retries are spent; count requests.

dimension: Upgrade and data compatibility; network etiquette (round 2 gap)
scenario: Settings > Privacy covers (clipboard, translate) were chosen on a newer build, then an older build (a worktree or an earlier release) is run, then the newer one again.
expected: A cover that was on stays on after the round trip.
actual_by_code: PrivacyMode.init (PrivacyMode.swift:65-83) upgrades 'everything covered' to 'everything that exists now' only by comparing the stored list with privacyKnownSections. The newer build writes known = all sections at every launch (:82). An older build that knows fewer sections rewrites privacyMode.sections as only what it knew, but cannot update the newer key. On return, restored.count (1) differs from existed.count (2) and the newer section (Translate) comes back uncovered. persist() keeps the legacy bool in step for rollback (:100-104), but not the list for roll-forward.
steps: Seed defaults with sections=[clipboard], known=[clipboard, translate]; init PrivacyMode; assert covers(.translate).

dimension: Upgrade and data compatibility; network etiquette (round 2 gap)
scenario: The Shelf's three parallel defaults arrays (shelf.urls, shelf.urls.bookmarks, shelf.urls.dates) are written by two different builds or by hand.

actual_by_code: storedURLs (ShelfStore.swift:143-165) pairs bookmarks with paths by index whenever the two counts are equal, and then trusts the bookmark's resolved URL over the path. An older or foreign writer that reorders or replaces entries but keeps the count (remove one, add one) makes card A resolve to card B's file. A different count discards all bookmarks silently. Dates are handled safely by a count check (load, ~:110). The current build always writes the arrays together (persist :420-442), so this arises only through mixed writers.

dimension: Upgrade and data compatibility; network etiquette (round 2 gap)
scenario: The keychain returns the access token but not the refresh token (or the reverse), for example when the data-protection keychain is locked at boot, on a build that also has a stale ad-hoc-era spotify-credentials.json.
expected: Credentials are read as one consistent generation.
actual_by_code: TokenStore.read tries the keychain and then the file for each account separately (TokenStore.swift:57-60). CredentialStore.readTokens reads expiresAt, accessToken and refreshToken one by one (SpotifyAccount.swift:548-550). A transient keychain miss for refreshToken falls through to the older file copy while the other fields come from the keychain. A rotated-out refresh token is then spent, which gets invalid_grant (and might revoke the family). The result is cached for the process lifetime (cache, :510, :557), so one bad read sticks. The leftover file after moving to the keychain is not cleared (ledger on TokenStore delete).
